summary: SIEM parity hashproof request and per-record header preservation for webhook audit stream
description: Issue summary: Customer requests a cryptographically verifiable alignment (hashproof) between Redwood audit events and their SIEM ingest (QRadar) plus strict preservation of per-request HTTP headers (x-request-id, x-forwarded-for, x-tenant-id) on every delivered event. Impact: Customer cannot reconcile order and origin of events for a regulatory forensics exercise; inability to prove event ordering and header context is blocking their compliance evidence package. Environment: prod (us-east) tenant 'hivebank-prod' using push webhook exporter to customer-owned QRadar HEC bridge. Request: 1) Provide a lightweight per-batch and per-record hash manifest (SHA256 hex strings) anchored to a rolling checkpoint so customer can demonstrate ordering and integrity. 2) Confirm and enable an option to guarantee preservation of request-level headers for each exported event (not stripped during batching/aggregation). 3) Share a sample evidence bundle (30-minute slice) that includes raw audit payloads, headers, and the accompanying hash manifest for QA and legal review.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant configured in console: export->webhook->push with 'batching' enabled, destination set to customer QRadar HEC endpoint behind their proxy. 2) Trigger activity sequence in tenant: create session, login, model inference calls (3 requests), delete session. 3) Observe that some delivered events do not contain x-request-id and x-forwarded-for in the HEC records when batching >1. 4) Compare ordering between Redwood audit sequence IDs and QRadar event timestamps; customer reports mismatches and no signed manifest for reconciliation.
logs:
Support collected delivery logs and exporter traces. Sample from delivery worker: 
[2026-03-10T14:02:35Z] deliverer-7: batch_id=b-78 size=3 dest=qradar-hec-01 status=200 preserved_headers=[x-tenant-id] missing=[x-request-id,x-forwarded-for] 
[2026-03-10T14:02:36Z] webhook-proxy: forwarded batch b-78 -> 10.10.5.34:3231 latency_ms=48
We also pulled the audit ledger entries: seq evt-20260310-0001..evt-0004 and raw JSON for the 30-minute window.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: batching code path normalizes/merges request headers and only emits tenant-level header on batch envelope. Confirmed by looking at delivery worker code and test logs. Evidence: reproduced in staging by toggling batching: with batching disabled, per-event headers are preserved; with batching enabled, header merging occurs. Additional finding: the manifest capability exists in a prototype form for S3 snapshot exports but not for webhook push. Proposed fix options: (A) Add a 'preserve_headers: true' flag that expands batch delivery to include per-record header sub-objects (non-breaking opt-in). (B) Implement a per-record hash manifest emitted as a companion file/endpoint for push (rolling checkpoint tokens). Engineering notes: PR #4123 implements header preservation behind a feature flag and emits per-batch manifest with per-record SHA256(hex) of canonicalized JSON. Staging tests show alignment: Redwood sequence order -> manifest hashes -> QRadar ingestion when customer uses provided mapping script. Risk: slight increase in payload size and delivery latency for large batches. Rollout plan: enable flag for hivebank-prod in staging, run parity test, then staged rollout to prod with monitoring.
comments: Priya Shah (Support) [2026-03-10]: Logged request and requested sample HEC parsing rules and a 30-minute window. Assigned to SRE for investigation.
Alice Mercer (HiveBank) [2026-03-10]: Provided HEC mapping and example QRadar parsing rule; noted that the compliance deadline is end of month and they require a signed artifact for auditors.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) [2026-03-11]: Confirmed reproduction in staging. Batching path merges headers. Opening engineering PR to add opt-in preservation and manifest emission (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123).

Liam O'Connor (SRE) [2026-03-12]: Deployed feature-flag to staging and ran parity test with HiveBank. All 120 sample events matched SHA256 manifest hashes and headers preserved. Customer validated parsing on their side and confirmed ordering reconciliation.
Alice Mercer (HiveBank) [2026-03-12]: Verified sample bundle in staging. Requested timeline for production rollout and an attestation note for their auditors.
resolution: Workaround provided: temporarily disable batching for hivebank-prod to guarantee per-event header preservation (applied by Support on 2026-03-11). Permanent fix: feature-flagged implementation of 'preserve_headers' and per-batch manifest with per-record SHA256 hashes merged to PR 4123. Staging validation passed 2026-03-12. Target production rollout: enable feature-flag for hivebank-prod on 2026-03-14 pending change review and canary monitoring. Deliverables to customer: 1) ZIP evidence bundle for requested 30-minute slice (raw events + headers + manifest + verification script). 2) Attestation note describing procedure and risk tradeoffs. Follow-ups: create INT ticket to add automated parity alerts (INT-22044) and update docs with header preservation option.
